newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk pipe firm Borusan sees '97 sales up.
newsitem.headline: Turk pipe firm Borusan sees '97 sales up.

text.p: Turkey's leading steel pipe producer Borusan Birlesik Boru Fabrikalari A.S. said on Thursday it expected a 10-percent rise in its total 1997 sales due to constant prices instead of an output rise.
"We expect a reinvigoration in markets in 1997. So we are targeting to raise our turnover by 10 percent on constant prices," General Manager Bulent Demircioglu said.
"Our profitability will also rise compared to this year," he told Reuters in an interview.

The company's total sales, which stood at 260,000 tonnes in the first nine months against a target of 250,000 tonnes, are expected to hit 290,000 tonnes at end-year with a $170 million turnover, he said.
Demircioglu said market conditions this year forced the company to target a low-income policy by volume sales during 1996 after a slowdown in late 1995.
"The markets were on the positive phase until the fourth quarter of 1995. Then we entered the negative phase, which pulled the prices down, about 30-35 percent," he said.
Borusan has an annual production capacity of 350,000 tonnes at its two plants -- in Istanbul and Gemlik. Its shares opened at 6,700 lira on Thursday, down from Wednesday's close at 6,800.
About 40 percent of the total 1997 sales will be exports, targeted mainly to Europe, the United States, North Africa, Russia and Far East.
Borusan's exports were 90,000 tonnes in the first nine months this year and were estimated to end the year at 120,000 tonnes, with a turnover of up to $68 million, Demircioglu said.
Borusan will have 11 percent profit margin before tax at the end of this year, less 14 percent than last year, Demircioglu said. He did not give other details on the company's profit.
He said Borusan would continue to spend up to $6 million a year for its investments.
"But we concentrate on modernisation investments, rather than capacity expansion to increase productivity, quality and service," he said.
By the end of this year, Borusan will increase output of "special steel pipes", used in car and machinery industries, to 10,000 tonnes annually from 3,500 tonnes now.
The company has recently begun producing polyethylene-coated pipes to carry natural gas to homes in Ankara and Istanbul.
